info.title: Thematiq
info.description: The JSON API of Thematiq, house style for Nextcloud: design tokens and token sets, overrides, custom CSS and components, fonts, icons and app brands, document styles, previews, scheduled switches, the audit trail and the admin settings. Public token, style and brand reads are under /api; the admin endpoints are under /settings.

Accepts `{ candidates: [{ name, value, role: "text"|"ui" }], background: string }` and returns `{ results: [{ name, ratio, threshold, level, pass, unevaluated? }] }`. A malformed request (missing/invalid `candidates` or `background`) returns 400, never a silent 200 with fabricated results.

get.summary: Declarative health check (ADR-006)
get.description:
Declarative health check (ADR-006).

Runs the manifest-declared checks through the AppHost engine and renders the `{status, app, version, checks}` envelope with the status code the engine's policy resolved. CORS headers are emitted only when the manifest opts in, exactly as the engine does.

When the AppHost engine cannot be resolved — openregister absent or disabled — the endpoint still answers (the whole point of a health probe): `status: degraded`, `checks.openregister: unavailable`, HTTP 200.

Liveness probe — no credential, so a ceiling and no counter.

200.description: `{status, app, version, checks}`.

get.summary: Expose Prometheus metrics
get.description:
Expose Prometheus metrics.

Deliberately NOT a #[PublicPage]: the metrics body exposes internal operational detail (token set name, override/theming-sync counts, exact PHP/Nextcloud versions) that should not be reachable by unauthenticated/anonymous requests. Without an explicit auth attribute the Nextcloud SecurityMiddleware default applies — admin-only — so a Prometheus scraper must authenticate as an admin (e.g. via an app password) to reach this endpoint.

200.description: Plain text response with Prometheus metrics.

get.description:

post.summary: Store the layout options: the workplace layout, the brand stripe and its placement, the navigation width, the selected navigation entry's style and the login watermark
post.description:
Store the layout options: the workplace layout, the brand stripe and its placement, the navigation width, the selected navigation entry's style and the login watermark.

Each option is read from the request parameter named in FIELDS: `workplaceLayout` (`default`, `light`), `brandStripe` (`1`, `0`), `navigationWidth` (a whole number of pixels, 200 to 480), `navigationActiveStyle` (`default`, `soft`), `brandStripePlacement` (`header-and-login`, `header`, `login`), `loginWatermark` (`1`, `0`) and `headerStyle` (`default`, `workplace`); empty or absent follows the theme.

Every value is validated before any is written, so a request with one bad value changes nothing. The answer carries the stored choices and what the instance-wide token set now resolves to, which is what the admin panel needs to add or drop the stylesheets on the open page.

200.description: The stored and the resolved state, or HTTP 400 on an unknown value.

post.summary: Set the Marianne acknowledgement gate
post.description: Set the Marianne acknowledgement gate. Disabling it reverts every subsequent render to Inter without deleting the bundled font files.

post.summary: Set whether Save overrides asks for confirmation first
post.description:
Set whether Save overrides asks for confirmation first.

Two flags, because the two questions are not the same one. On the stock `nextcloud` set there is a real choice to make — keep the edits as a new token set, or write them over the running Nextcloud theme — and on any other set there is only a confirmation. An admin who has stopped wanting one has not necessarily stopped wanting the other.

Both default to ON. The dialogs offer "do not ask again", and the pair of controls under the token editor turns them back on, so the choice is never one-way.

post.summary: Import a design-system theme (or a finished token set) as a custom set
post.description:
Import a design-system theme (or a finished token set) as a custom set.

Accepts a `name` plus EITHER a multipart `file` or a `content` paste — identical from the read onward, because a theme usually arrives as text in a clipboard, not as a file on disk. The content is CONVERTED first (`TokenSetConverterService`, which detects which of the four accepted shapes it is from the content itself, never from the file name), and the converter's emitted CSS is then put through the existing validator and stored as `css/tokens/custom-{slug}.css`.

Conversion runs BEFORE validation, never instead of it: the validator is still the last gate on the bytes that get written.

THE CONVERTER IS WIRED IN UNCONDITIONALLY, ON PURPOSE, AND IS NOT FINISHED. There is no feature flag and no bypass, because the path it replaces was strictly worse: it accepted only pre-baked `--nldesign-*` CSS, so every other shape a design system publishes — a W3C Design Tokens document, a Style Dictionary `tokens.json`, a built theme stylesheet — was simply refused. The converter accepts all four and is already better than what was here before, which is why it ships now rather than behind a flag nobody would turn on.

What is NOT yet done, and is tracked in `openspec/changes/nlds-theme-converter`: the parity tests between this runtime and its JS mirror, the paste box, the report rendering in the admin panel, and regenerating the shipped sets. Until those land, expect conversions to need review — the emitted file is validated, so nothing unsafe is written, but "it stored something" is not yet "it stored the right thing".

200.description: `{ id, imported, skipped, warnings, report, counts, inputKind }` or an error.

get.summary: The set as a DTCG download: only what the set's own file declares
